summary: Risk-off overnight: the Dow fell about 1,100 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq about 2% (S&P's 6th straight loss) as hawkish FOMC minutes pushed December Fed hike odds near 95%, with Nvidia CEO fallout and Anthropic's IPO weighing on tech. The dollar stayed firm, USD/JPY sits near 160 under intervention watch, and Japan CPI is due at 10:30am Sydney.
events_next_24h: Sat 1:45am USD S&P Global flash PMIs (Nov)
tier1_next_14d: US PCE and personal income (Oct) + Q3 GDP 2nd estimate · Thu, 26 Nov, 12:30am

ES.why: Hawkish Fed minutes put a December hike near 95% and the S&P fell ~2% for a 6th straight loss; fund positioning is neutral, not stretched.
ES.risk: A soft flash PMI or Fed pushback on hikes could spark a sharp oversold bounce.

NQ.why: Rate-hike fears and Nvidia CEO fallout hit tech ~2%; funds were crowded long (98th pct) so there are longs left to unwind.
NQ.risk: Oversold with VXN at 98th pct; a dovish Fed headline or strong Anthropic trading could trigger a squeeze.

YM.why: The Dow dropped about 1,100 points on hike fears, a broad selloff, not just tech.
YM.risk: Any easing in Fed hike pricing or a big rebound in defensives.

RTY.why: Small caps are most sensitive to higher borrowing costs as the Fed leans toward hiking again; lean only, no RTY-specific data found.
RTY.risk: A drop in yields after weak data would help small caps most.

NKD.why: Wall Street's 2% fall and a December BOJ hike in view weigh on Japan stocks already down 8% in 20 days; funds are neutral.
NKD.risk: A hot Japan CPI shift, yen intervention or a US futures rebound in Asia could flip it.

6E.why: Euro is stuck under 1.10 as Fed hike pricing keeps the dollar bid even on weak US data.
6E.risk: Strong euro-area flash PMIs or a fall in US yields.

6J.why: Fed hikes widen the US-Japan rate gap (yen down) but intervention risk near 160, a December BOJ hike and risk-off pull the other way.
6J.risk: Confirmed intervention would send the yen sharply stronger; a break above 160 USD/JPY the opposite.

6B.why: BoE hiked to 4.00% in early November but the dollar is firm; no fresh UK driver found overnight.
6B.risk: UK flash PMIs or BoE speaker surprises.

6A.why: Australian unemployment jumped to 4.9%, raising doubts about the RBA, and risk-off weighs on the Aussie.
6A.risk: A rebound in global stocks or strong China news.

ZN.why: Fed hike talk pushes yields up, but stock-market fear sends money into Treasuries; yields only ticked lower overnight.
ZN.risk: A hot flash PMI price index (bearish ZN) or deeper equity rout (bullish ZN).

GC.why: Gold held steady after hawkish minutes: a firm dollar and hike odds weigh, Iran risk supports, and funds lean short (21st pct).
GC.risk: A clear break in the dollar or a Middle East escalation.

CL.why: Brent slipped toward $92 on surplus talk while Hormuz attacks persist; funds are crowded short (10th pct), so downside is crowded.
CL.risk: A new Hormuz incident could squeeze shorts; a peace deal would drop prices.
